market_summary: A second losing week for growth: in the week to Fri Oct 23 the S&P 500 fell 0.5% to 7,623.68 and the Nasdaq 0.7% to 25,955.34, while the Dow (+0.4%) and Russell 2000 (+2.0%) rose. The damage was in chips: the SOX fell more than 6% on Thu Oct 22 after Lam Research flagged supply constraints, on top of worries about AI funding and credit (Marvell -9%, Intel -7% that day), and Tesla's Q3 showed operating income down 56% y/y with capex lower than Q2. Money moved into bonds, so the 10-year fell 8bp on the week to 5.00% even as Brent rose about 5% to roughly $116, its highest since June 2022, on fears of renewed US strikes on Iran with Hormuz navigation still unresolved. Futures put the chance of a hike this week at about 9% (rates held at 3.75-4.00%), with a December hike still priced. Energy-for-AI stayed strong: Bloom Energy grew Q3 revenue 138% and raised guidance for the third time this year. Brazil's Oct 25 runoff was still undecided at publication, with Lula narrowly ahead at about two-thirds counted. Next: Robinhood Q3 Wed Oct 28 ~07:00 AEDT; Enphase Wed Oct 28 morning AEDT; Fed decision Thu Oct 29 05:00 AEDT; Apple Mac event Thu Oct 29 04:00 AEDT; Alphabet and Microsoft Thu Oct 29 morning AEDT; BYD Q3 Thu Oct 29 evening AEDT; US GDP/PCE Thu Oct 29 23:30 AEDT; Amazon and Intel Fri Oct 30 morning AEDT.

AMZN.reason: Down 5% since Oct 21 in the Meta-led AI capex selloff. Q3 results Thu Oct 29 after close (~7am AEDT Fri Oct 30); AWS growth vs capex is the test.

AXOS.reason: Up 2% since Oct 21, steady while tech sold off. Fiscal Q1 results Thu Oct 29 after close, call ~8am AEDT Fri Oct 30.

BABA.reason: Down 5% since Oct 21 after China's market regulator told e-commerce platforms to tighten quality controls, hitting livestream and quick retail. Results Nov 24.

ENPH.reason: Down 1% since Oct 21. Q3 results Tue Oct 27 after close (~7am AEDT Wed Oct 28); Q4 guidance matters most.

FIGR.reason: Down 9% since Oct 21 with no company-specific bad news; small business lending hit a first $100M quarter. Q3 results Nov 12 pre-market (~12:30am AEDT Nov 13).

GOOGL.reason: Down 4% since Oct 21 on AI spending worries. Q3 results Wed Oct 28 after close (~7am AEDT Thu Oct 29); Cloud growth vs capex is the test.

LDI.reason: Up about 15% since Oct 21 as Treasury yields fell sharply. Q3 date not yet announced; early November likely. Small, high-risk position.

META.reason: Down 8% since Oct 21: Q3 beat and Q4 guide fine, but capex raised, free cash flow negative, buybacks paused and a new non-voting share class coming.

MRVL.reason: Down 7% since Oct 21 after an 8.7% drop on Oct 22 tied to Meta capex and Lam Research supply warnings. Credit facility doubled to $3B.

MU.reason: Down 4% since Oct 21 in the chip selloff. Taoyuan strike was 11 officials, no output hit; talks resume Mon Oct 27 after members rejected the offer.

NFLX.reason: Up 1% since Oct 21 after the post-earnings drop on a cut ad forecast and softer Q4 guide. Down 29% this year; wait for a base.

NVDA.reason: Down 5% since Oct 21 in the AI capex scare, no company-specific news. Demand still exceeds supply, including China RTX PRO 5500 orders.

RKT.reason: Up 6% since Oct 21 as yields dropped. Q3 results Thu Oct 29, call 4:30pm ET (~7:30am AEDT Fri Oct 30).

TSM.reason: Down 3% since Oct 21 in the chip selloff after a record quarter. Lam's supply warning points to tight capacity, which favours TSMC pricing.

STRIPE.reason: No new tender or round reported since the $159B February 2026 tender. Mark unchanged.

OPENAI.reason: Reported near a ~$30B raise at $1.25T pre-money, cut from $1.4T after investor pushback. Not closed, so mark stays at the March round.

headlines: Meta's capex raise and Lam's supply warning hit chips: SOX fell 6.7% Oct 22; Meta down 8%, Marvell 7% since Oct 21.
Mortgage names rose as the 10-year fell to 5.00%: loanDepot up about 15%, Rocket 6% since Oct 21.
Brent hit about $116, its highest since June 2022; futures give a Fed hike this week only about 9%.
Bloom Q3 revenue up 138% with guidance raised again; moved to accumulate. Credo cut to low conviction on new competition.
OpenAI reported near a $30B raise at $1.25T, below its $1.4T target; not closed, so the mark is unchanged.
This week, all morning AEDT: Enphase Wed; Fed, Alphabet, Microsoft Thu; Amazon, Axos, Rocket Fri.
